claim: The Virtual Embryo from the Berkeley Drosophila Transcription Network Project is a cellular resolution, spatiotemporal atlas of gene expression and morphology for a whole Drosophila melanogaster blastoderm embryo.
source_text: The Virtual Embryo from the Berkeley Drosophila Transcription Network Project provides the best available data for this purpose (Fowlkes et al., 2008). It is a cellular resolution, spatiotemporal atlas of gene expression and morphology for a whole Drosophila melanogaster blastoderm embryo.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by a citation to Fowlkes et al., 2008, which describes the Virtual Embryo dataset.

claim: The Virtual Embryo dataset contains three-dimensional coordinates for 6078 nuclei.
source_text: The dataset contains the three-dimensional coordinates for 6078 nuclei, along with mRNA expression measurements of 95 different genes at six time points during the 50 min leading to gastrulation
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by the dataset description, which provides specific numerical data about the number of nuclei.

claim: The Virtual Embryo dataset contains mRNA expression measurements of 95 different genes at six time points during the 50 min leading to gastrulation.
source_text: The dataset contains the three-dimensional coordinates for 6078 nuclei, along with mRNA expression measurements of 95 different genes at six time points during the 50 min leading to gastrulation
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by the dataset description, providing specific information about gene measurements and time points.

claim: eve is expressed in a symmetrical pattern of seven stripes that subdivide the embryo along the anteroposterior axis.
source_text: eve is expressed in a symmetrical pattern of seven stripes that subdivide the embryo along the anteroposterior axis (Nüsslein-Volhard and Wieschaus, 1980).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by a citation to Nüsslein-Volhard and Wieschaus, 1980, and represents established scientific knowledge about eve expression.

claim: Each eve stripe is only a few nuclei wide.
source_text: Each stripe is only a few nuclei wide and any regulatory input function of an enhancer must define at least two borders at a high level of precision.
evidence_reasoning: This claim draws from established knowledge about the spatial characteristics of eve stripes.

claim: The enhancer eve 2 controls stripe 2 of eve expression.
source_text: Here, we focus on the enhancers eve 2 and eve 3+7, which have been shown to control stripe 2 and stripes 3 and 7 respectively (Goto et al., 1989; Harding et al., 1989; Stanojevic et al., 1991; Small et al., 1992, 1996).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by multiple citations and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: The enhancer eve 3+7 controls stripes 3 and 7 of eve expression.
source_text: Here, we focus on the enhancers eve 2 and eve 3+7, which have been shown to control stripe 2 and stripes 3 and 7 respectively (Goto et al., 1989; Harding et al., 1989; Stanojevic et al., 1991; Small et al., 1992, 1996).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by multiple citations and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: eve stripe 2 is controlled by the gap genes.
source_text: Through detailed molecular analysis, it is known that eve stripe 2 is controlled by the gap genes (Frasch and Levine, 1987; Stanojevic et al., 1991; Small et al., 1992)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by multiple citations and represents established knowledge about eve stripe 2 regulation.

claim: Hunchback (Hb) and Bicoid (Bcd) are activators that enable broad permissive eve expression in the region of stripe 2.
source_text: In the generally accepted minimal mechanism, two activators Hunchback (Hb) and Bicoid (Bcd) enable broad permissive eve expression in the region of stripe 2, while two repressors Giant (Gt) and Kruppel (Kr) define the anterior and posterior borders respectively by suppressing eve outside the stripe.
evidence_reasoning: This claim represents the generally accepted mechanism in the field, drawing from established scientific knowledge.

claim: Giant (Gt) and Kruppel (Kr) are repressors that define the anterior and posterior borders of eve stripe 2 respectively by suppressing eve outside the stripe.
source_text: In the generally accepted minimal mechanism, two activators Hunchback (Hb) and Bicoid (Bcd) enable broad permissive eve expression in the region of stripe 2, while two repressors Giant (Gt) and Kruppel (Kr) define the anterior and posterior borders respectively by suppressing eve outside the stripe.
evidence_reasoning: This claim represents the generally accepted mechanism in the field, drawing from established scientific knowledge.

claim: The logistic model using Bcd, Hb, Gt, and Kr accurately recapitulates eve stripe 2 expression across the entire embryo.
source_text: To the best of our knowledge, this the first time that eve 2's expression has been predicted so accurately across the entire embryo including the anteriormost region. Most nuclei inside the stripe are correctly classified as having a high probability of being ON, and there is minimal 'over-spill' either side of the stripe
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by the model predictions and data analysis presented in the manuscript, including quantitative measurements in Table 1.

claim: The four standard regulators of eve 2 (Bcd, Hb, Gt, Kr) encode dorsoventral curvature information, implying that dorsoventral factors are not required to provide this information directly to eve 2.
source_text: The model defines eve expression around the entire circumference of the embryo, following the dorsal-ventral curvature of the stripe: this demonstrates that the four standard regulators of eve 2 already encode this information, implying that dorsoventral factors are not required to provide this information directly to eve 2.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on the model's ability to predict dorsoventral curvature using only the four regulators, leading to an inference about the sufficiency of these factors.

claim: The linear logistic model identifies 86% of nuclei in stripe 2 as having high probability of being ON.
source_text: Table 1. Measurements quantifying the accuracy of eve 2 predictions... eve 2 linear logistic 86 23 2
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by quantitative data presented in Table 1.

claim: The quadratic logistic model identifies 93% of nuclei in stripe 2 as having high probability of being ON.
source_text: Table 1. Measurements quantifying the accuracy of eve 2 predictions... eve 2 quadratic logistic 93 21 2
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by quantitative data presented in Table 1.

claim: The quadratic logistic model provides a slightly more accurate fit to the data than the linear model for eve stripe 2.
source_text: Though both linear and quadratic models output excellent predictions, the latter provides a slightly more accurate fit to the data.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by comparison of the quantitative accuracy measurements in Table 1.

claim: The linear model identifies Bcd as a repressor of eve stripe 2, whereas most existing literature defines the TF as an activator.
source_text: The linear model successfully recapitulates stripe 2 expression; however, it identifies Bcd as a repressor, whereas most existing literature defines the TF as an activator.
evidence_reasoning: This claim compares the model output (data) with established literature (knowledge), highlighting a discrepancy.

claim: The need for Bcd-binding sites for successful eve expression suggests an activating function for Bcd.
source_text: The need for Bcd-binding sites for successful eve expression suggests an activating function (Small et al., 1992)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by a citation to Small et al., 1992, which provides experimental evidence.

claim: The eve 2 enhancer is inactive in the anteriormost region of the embryo despite Bcd being present at high concentrations and the known repressors Gt and Kr having low concentrations.
source_text: but this does not explain why the enhancer is inactive in the anteriormost region of the embryo despite Bcd being present at high concentrations and the known repressors Gt and Kr having low concentrations
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on observed expression patterns (data) and known regulator distributions (knowledge).

claim: A quadratic term for Bcd enables the model to reconcile Bcd's dual regulatory function as both a repressor in the anterior and an activator in the region of stripe 2.
source_text: The result is clear: the modified model retains a repressive function for Bcd in the anterior of the embryo where it is present in high concentrations, but enables an activating function in the region of stripe 2 where it has lower concentrations
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by the model predictions showing concentration-dependent regulatory effects.

claim: The quadratic model for eve 2 predicts that loss of gt causes eve expression to extend towards the anterior of the embryo, in excellent agreement with experimental evidence.
source_text: Loss of (A) gt or (B) Kr causes eve expression to extend towards the anterior and posterior of the embryo respectively, in excellent agreement with experimental evidence.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by model predictions (data) that match experimental results (citation to Small et al., 1992).

claim: The quadratic model for eve 2 predicts that loss of Kr causes eve expression to extend towards the posterior of the embryo, in excellent agreement with experimental evidence.
source_text: Loss of (A) gt or (B) Kr causes eve expression to extend towards the anterior and posterior of the embryo respectively, in excellent agreement with experimental evidence.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by model predictions (data) that match experimental results (citation to Small et al., 1992).

claim: The quadratic model predicts that perturbing hb leads to complete loss of eve stripe 2.
source_text: (D) Perturbing hb leads to complete loss of eve stripe 2 for both models.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is directly supported by the model predictions shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The measured concentrations of Hb (protein) and kni (mRNA) alone are not sufficient for models of stripe 3 and 7 expression.
source_text: The measured concentrations of Hb (protein) and kni (mRNA) alone are not sufficient for our models of stripe 3 and 7 expression; in particular, the concentration of Hb is too low to repress expression to the posterior of stripe 7
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by the model fitting results showing insufficient predictive power with only these two regulators.

claim: Kni is thought to repress the region between eve stripes 3 and 7.
source_text: Kni is thought to repress the region between the stripes and Hb is thought to repress in the anterior and posterior regions outside the stripes (Clyde et al., 2003).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by a citation and represents established knowledge about Kni function.

claim: Hb is thought to repress in the anterior and posterior regions outside eve stripes 3 and 7.
source_text: Kni is thought to repress the region between the stripes and Hb is thought to repress in the anterior and posterior regions outside the stripes (Clyde et al., 2003).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by a citation and represents established knowledge about Hb function.

claim: The linear model for eve 3+7 includes Hb, kni, tll, and Gt as regulators.
source_text: (A–C) The linear model including Hb, kni, tll, and Gt
evidence_reasoning: This claim describes the composition of the linear model as presented in the manuscript.

claim: The quadratic model for eve 3+7 comprises Hb, kni, and tll, with a quadratic term for Hb as a concentration-dependent dual regulator.
source_text: (D–F) the quadratic model comprises Hb, kni, and tll, with a quadratic term for Hb as a concentration-dependent dual regulator.
evidence_reasoning: This claim describes the composition of the quadratic model as presented in the manuscript.

claim: The quadratic model for eve 3+7 defines sharper stripe borders than the linear model.
source_text: Both models clearly define the two stripes, though the midline ribbon plots show that the quadratic model defines the sharpest borders.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by visual comparison of model predictions shown in the figures.

claim: The quadratic model for eve 3+7 is simpler than the linear model, requiring only three regulators compared to four.
source_text: First, it is simpler: the quadratic requires only three regulators, compared to four in the linear model.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on direct comparison of the model compositions.

claim: The quadratic model for eve 3+7 is more robust to the choice of training data than the linear model.
source_text: Third, the quadratic model is more robust to the choice of training data (Figure 4—figure supplement 3), indicating that it describes the regulatory relationship uniformly across the embryo
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by cross-validation results shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 3.

claim: In the kni mutant, expression of an eve 3+7 reporter transgene extends fully between the two stripes before partially retreating towards wild-type expression.
source_text: In the kni mutant, expression of an eve 3+7 reporter transgene extends fully between the two stripes before partially retreating towards wild-type expression (Small et al., 1996).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by a citation to Small et al., 1996, describing experimental observations.

claim: When Kni-binding sites in the eve 3+7 enhancer are removed, the expression pattern matches the kni null mutant.
source_text: Similarly, when Kni-binding sites in the eve 3+7 enhancer are removed, the expression pattern matches the kni null mutant (Struffi et al., 2011)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by a citation to Struffi et al., 2011, describing experimental results.

claim: The linear model for eve 3+7 predicts full extension between the two stripes when kni is eliminated.
source_text: To mimic both of these types of perturbations, we eliminated kni as an input. Under these conditions, the linear model predicts the observed full extension between the two stripes, whereas the quadratic does not
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by the model predictions shown in Figure 5A.

claim: There is strong evidence that kni is a repressor of hb, as its loss causes hb expression to extend from stripe 7 towards stripe 3.
source_text: There is strong evidence that kni is a repressor of hb, as its loss causes hb expression to extend from stripe 7 towards stripe 3 (Hülskamp et al., 1990; Clyde et al., 2003).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to experimental studies showing the regulatory relationship.

claim: In embryos null for hb zygotic expression, eve stripe 3 moves anteriorly and expands, whereas stripe 7 shows more limited widening.
source_text: In embryos null for hb zygotic expression, eve stripe 3 moves anteriorly and expands, whereas stripe 7 shows more limited widening (Small et al., 1996).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by a citation to Small et al., 1996, describing experimental observations.

claim: Mutating Hb-binding sites in the eve 3+7 enhancer leads to expansion of stripe 3, though perhaps without the anterior shift.
source_text: Mutating Hb-binding sites in the eve 3+7 enhancer leads to similar expansion, though perhaps without the anterior shift of stripe 3 (Struffi et al., 2011).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by a citation to Struffi et al., 2011, describing experimental results.

claim: Maternally deposited hb mRNA is ubiquitous but differentially translated in the anterior.
source_text: Maternally deposited hb mRNA is ubiquitous but differentially translated in the anterior (Hülskamp et al., 1989).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by a citation to Hülskamp et al., 1989, describing the distribution of maternal hb.

claim: Zygotically, hb is transcribed in both an anterior domain that largely overlaps the maternal hb pattern and in a posterior stripe.
source_text: Zygotically, hb is transcribed in both an anterior domain that largely overlaps the maternal hb pattern and in a posterior stripe (Margolis et al., 1995).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by a citation to Margolis et al., 1995, describing zygotic hb expression.

claim: The quadratic models predict the fine-scale effects of misexpression experiments with remarkable accuracy whereas the linear models do not.
source_text: The quadratic models predict the fine-scale effects of this misexpression experiment with remarkable accuracy whereas the linear models do not
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by comparison of model predictions to experimental results shown in Figure 7.

claim: The quadratic model trained on stripe 3 successfully reproduces the bending and bulging of both stripes 3 and 7 under hb misexpression.
source_text: Specifically, the quadratic model trained on stripe 3 successfully reproduces the bending and bulging of both stripes 3 and 7 under hb misexpression (Figure 7B)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by the model predictions shown in Figure 7B compared to experimental images.

claim: The quadratic model trained on stripe 3 successfully reproduces the repression seen with kni misexpression.
source_text: Specifically, the quadratic model trained on stripe 3 successfully reproduces the bending and bulging of both stripes 3 and 7 under hb misexpression (Figure 7B), as well as the repression seen with kni misexpression (Figure 7A).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by the model predictions shown in Figure 7A compared to experimental images.

claim: Simple functional forms relating TF concentrations to eve expression outputs are highly predictive of wild-type and mutant expression patterns.
source_text: We showed that simple functional forms relating TF concentrations to eve expression outputs are highly predictive of wild-type and mutant expression patterns.
evidence_reasoning: This claim summarizes the overall findings of the study, supported by the various model predictions and validations presented.

claim: Precise positional information is available in the early embryo.
source_text: In doing so, we have demonstrated that precise positional information—in other words, information interpreted by individual nuclei to produce an expression pattern—is available in the early embryo.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is inferred from the success of the models in predicting precise expression patterns using only TF concentrations.

claim: The combined action of multiple morphogens and a corresponding interpretative threshold is able to read positional information from measured gradients alone.
source_text: Our model, however, shows that the combined action of multiple morphogens and a corresponding interpretative threshold is indeed able to read positional information from measured gradients alone.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is inferred from the model's ability to predict expression patterns using combinations of TF concentrations.

claim: Activators and repressors contribute symmetrically to positional information: they work to increase or decrease the probability of transcription, but neither class acts separately according to a threshold that is independent of the concentrations of other factors.
source_text: In particular, activators and repressors contribute symmetrically to positional information: they work to increase or decrease the probability of transcription, but neither class acts separately according to a threshold that is independent of the concentrations of other factors.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is inferred from the structure and behavior of the logistic regression models.

claim: Synergistic effects can be observed with a linear combination of concentrations without any pairwise interactions between TFs.
source_text: Our model shows that this effect is observed with a linear combination of concentrations: that is, without any pairwise interactions between Hb and Bcd or other factors.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is inferred from the success of linear models that do not include explicit pairwise interaction terms.

claim: The success of the model without pairwise interactions suggests that the ordering and exact spacing of binding sites are not important, except potentially in the case of dual regulation.
source_text: Therefore, the success of our model without pairwise interactions suggests that the ordering and exact spacing of binding sites are not important, except potentially in the case of dual regulation.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is inferred from the model structure and its predictive success without explicit spatial binding site information.

claim: Hb has a dual role: it acts as a repressor in some enhancers (e.g., eve 3+7) and an activator in others (e.g. eve 2).
source_text: Hb has a dual role: it acts as a repressor in some enhancers (e.g., eve 3+7) and an activator in others (e.g. eve 2) (Small et al., 1992, 1996).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations and represents established knowledge about Hb function in different contexts.

claim: Including a quadratic term for Hb in the eve 3+7 model produces better wild-type predictions.
source_text: In our model of eve 3+7, including a quadratic term for concentration-dependent dual regulation produces better wild-type predictions, explains experimental perturbations accurately (with certain assumptions), and produces consistent fits across different training subsets.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by comparison of model performance metrics and visual predictions.

claim: Concentration-dependent regulatory activities have been observed in other systems, such as Sp1 regulation of the folate receptor gene in humans.
source_text: Concentration-dependent regulatory activities have been observed in other systems: for instance in humans, at low concentrations, Sp1 is as an activator of the folate receptor gene in conjunction with Ets TFs; at higher concentrations it becomes a repressor by blocking Ets binding (Kelley et al., 2003).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by a citation to Kelley et al., 2003, providing an example from another biological system.

claim: This is the first time that eve 2's expression has been predicted accurately across the entire embryo including the anteriormost region.
source_text: To the best of our knowledge, this the first time that eve 2's expression has been predicted so accurately across the entire embryo including the anteriormost region.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on the model's performance and comparison to previous modeling efforts in the literature.

claim: Modeling pair-rule expression accurately across the whole embryo has remained a significant challenge.
source_text: It is notable that though there has been some success in simulating the simpler gap gene expression pattern and in predicting eve expression on a portion of the anteroposterior axis, modeling pair-rule expression accurately across the whole embryo has remained a significant challenge (Jaeger et al., 2004; Janssens et al., 2006; Papatsenko and Levine, 2008; Segal et al., 2008; Kazemian et al., 2010; Kim et al., 2013).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by multiple citations documenting the state of the field.

claim: The Virtual Embryo dataset contains expression measurements normalized to a range of 0 to just over 1 across the entire embryo and time points.
source_text: The Virtual Embryo dataset contains expression measurements normalized to a range of 0 to just over 1 across the entire embryo and time points; thus 0.2 corresponds to ∼20% of the maximal expression.
evidence_reasoning: This claim describes the data normalization method used in the Virtual Embryo dataset.

claim: All models were trained using the third time point corresponding to ∼30 min before gastrulation.
source_text: All models were trained using the third time point corresponding to ∼30 min before gastrulation, when according to the Virtual Embryo data, the borders are sharpening and the stripes are not moving dramatically
evidence_reasoning: This claim describes the specific time point chosen for model training based on the dataset.

claim: Four pair-rule genes (fushi tarazu, odd skipped, hairy and paired) were excluded from the dataset.
source_text: Four pair-rule genes (fushi tarazu, odd skipped, hairy and paired) that have similar stripe patterns to eve were excluded from the data set

source_text: Moreover, eve expression looks qualitatively normal in these TF mutants (Schroeder et al., 2011).
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by a citation to Schroeder et al., 2011, providing experimental evidence.

source_text: Finally, it is notable that the model predicts a small amount of expression near stripe 7; ectopic expression of stripe 7 is sometimes observed in transgenic reporters driven by eve 2 enhancers (Small et al., 1992; Janssens et al., 2006; Hare et al., 2008).

source_text: Gratifyingly, the best-scoring model comprises the known regulators Hb, Bcd, Gt, and Kr.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on the regulator discovery analysis that scored all possible models.

claim: The models extend from the posterior of stripe 7 to the anterior of the embryo, covering approximately 404 μm along the anteroposterior axis.
source_text: The coordinates of the Virtual Embryo are along the anteroposterior (x), left-right (y) and dorsoventral (z) axes. The difference between the minimum and maximum is 404 μm for the x-coordinate
evidence_reasoning: This claim is implicit in the description of the coordinate system and the extent of the embryo covered by the models.
